correctness.rationale: For size-one/two S5 equivalence classes, knowledge is Boolean box over an involution. An induction identifies E^k(X) with the radius-k ball inclusion predicate. An excluded furthest vertex proves the diameter cutoff is minimal. Two edge-disjoint matchings produce only alternating paths and cycles, apart from the isolated double-edge component. Connected labelled counts are j! for paths of size j and (2j-1)! for even cycles of size 2j (including the double edge when j=1). The labelled exponential formula gives the exact finite-depth series and \(n!\) extremal paths. Exhaustive independent integer/rational checks for \(1\le n\le7\) and valuations n=1..4 agree; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General classical common-knowledge reachability and finite-model complexity results strictly include the elementary observation that iteration depth is a graph distance. They do not imply the displayed labelled count without the restricted two-involution enumeration. The 2026 paper establishes broad modal results, not the exact restricted-size combinatorial numbers.

value.rationale: The exact least common-knowledge unrolling depth is a canonical modal-model invariant. Restricting information blocks to binary uncertainty is natural and makes the full n-by-depth distribution nontrivially enumerable. The formula predicts every labelled count and sharply identifies exactly \(n!\) maximum-depth frames for \(n\ge3\). It supports exact depth-bounded model-checking thresholds and enumerated benchmark populations; the restricted distribution is not a textbook reformulation of Zenger’s finite-model and translation theorems.
